clue.text: Love writer, old hat, is not otherwise unsettled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
a pen is a writing instrument
a toque is a small brimless hat of a style long worn, here the 'old hat'

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of 'is not' are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A romantic novelist in a dated hat is disturbed by something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges the letters of 'is not' to finish the answer. 'Old hat' looks like a phrase meaning stale, but it names an actual hat, a toque.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter still open to dispute is unresolved, so unsettled.

clue.text: Agricultural workers left out of joke

indicators.note: out of signals that something is missing from the word for joke

parts.note: a pleasantry is a light joking remark

explanation.surface: Farm labourers are excluded from the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry are the rural class who work the land.

parts.note: not is the word of negation
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A goal scored by an unhelpful partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut a nick in it, and a notch is such a cut.

clue.text: Deceased man, as they say, with his eyes open

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, 'died', seen on gravestones
'man' is a common way of saying manservant, a servant

explanation.surface: A dead man, people say, still has his eyes open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as they say' tells you that 'man' is meant in the idiomatic sense of a servant, as in 'my man will see to it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone watchful who notices everything goes about with eyes open.

indicators.note: turned signals the letters of 'about' are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat comes about and changes direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the world wars is a seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Theological offence against church property: note where one lies

parts.note: a sin is an offence against religious law
glebe is land owned by a parish church to support its clergyman
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A list of religious wrongs committed against a church's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' just sets the pieces side by side. GLEBE is an old English term for land that belongs to a parish living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed for one person is a place to sleep.

clue.text: Compiler's a long time with his supposed persona

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who says I'm, 'I am'
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: The setter talks of the long years spent building a public character.
explanation.definitionFit: A public image is the impression of oneself that others are meant to hold.

parts.note: a nob is slang for a person of high social rank
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A lord goes off to university while people go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no loaf in the house is a lack of the staple of the table.

clue.text: Writer turns up to use axe on relation

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: An author arrives to attack a family member with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relative.

parts.note: ex- marks something former
a bill becomes an act when passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the police, the Old Bill, approvingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Old Bill' is British slang for the police, but here 'old' and 'Bill' work separately. 'Nice' is used in its older sense of precise, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice distinction is a fine, precise one.

clue.text: Heartless shorthorn, young, doesn't like strong wind

indicators.note: heartless means the inner part of the word shorthorn is cut out

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep

explanation.surface: A cattle breed, fed up and youthful, dislikes gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes RTHO from the inside of SHORTHORN. The definition refers to the proverb 'God tempers the wind to the shorn lamb'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the wind is softened for a newly clipped young sheep, which would suffer in a gale.

clue.text: Put the fire on for the lady Erica

parts.note: to heat a room is to put the fire on
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Turn on the fire for a woman called Erica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica' looks like a woman's name but is the botanical genus of heath plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name of heaths, the low moorland shrubs.

parts.note: TNT, the explosive, is short for trinitro- plus a liquid solvent; the T that comes after T and N in that abbreviation stands for that solvent

explanation.surface: A chemical cleaner comes after the letters TN.
explanation.walkthrough: TNT abbreviates trinitrotoluene: T(ri)N(itro)T(oluene). The solvent is what the final T stands for, the letter following TN.
explanation.definitionFit: This liquid hydrocarbon is a common industrial solvent and the base of TNT.

definitions.meaning: G. F. ... was a Victorian English painter and sculptor
units of electrical power are named after James Watt

explanation.definitionFit: G. F. Watts painted 'Hope'; electrical power is measured in units named after Watt.

clue.text: Sailor in US city announces his engagement

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the city name

parts.note: Seattle is a city in Washington State
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman in an American city tells everyone he is getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' looks like a betrothal but means a battle; 'announces his' is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a fight between forces, here fought between fleets.

clue.text: Appeal to travellers, first getting fat without a lot of work

parts.note: A is first, as in A1 or grade A

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fat goes around the work

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word for work

parts.note: labour is work

explanation.surface: A call to passengers to put on weight with little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last two letters of the word for work, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the fat wraps around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The conductor's cry calling passengers onto the train or ship before departure.

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are put in a wrong order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet behaves nobly, or a doctor wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges NOBLY, OR and DR. 'nobly' hints that the poet was a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet who wrote Don Juan.

clue.text: Insect takes one watery expanse to another

parts.note: an ant is an insect
the Arctic is one of the world's oceans

explanation.surface: An insect sets off across one sea towards another.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant takes one ocean, the ARCTIC, to make another ocean; 19 Down continues the run with a third.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southern Ocean around the South Pole is a different ocean from the northern one.

clue.text: Man with money coming from the same party

indicators.note: the answer is made out of, so comes from, the letters of 'same party' reworked

explanation.surface: A rich man comes from the same political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official who hands out wages.
The ocean between Asia and the Americas; also an adjective for calm and peaceable.

annotationWithheld.clue: Given piece of land in Umtali

indicators.note: about means the joke goes around the people

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, as in bon mot
men are people

explanation.surface: A gag about very important persons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the people inside the joke; 'of importance' reads as describing the people, but 'importance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of great moment is one of great significance.

indicators.note: in places the universal letter inside the cellist's name

parts.note: Pablo Casals was a famous Catalan cellist
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Relaxed clothes, worn everywhere, on a concert musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Casuals are everyday clothes rather than formal dress.

parts.note: a single step that takes you a little higher up from floor level

explanation.surface: A route rising from the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A step in a staircase raises you from floor level toward the next floor.
A scrap is a fragment of paper or food, and also a scuffle.

clue.text: Stiffened cloth for two male beasts

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Coarse fabric meant for a pair of male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two male beasts' gives two pieces, BUCK and RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is coarse linen stiffened with glue, used in bookbinding.

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Performers attending an English lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank.

parts.note: flatter means duller, more lacking in interest
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A toady attends a rather dull king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns with insincere praise to win favour.

definitions.meaning: split in two, the word describes something someone has occupied as a seat

explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy fabric; read as SAT IN it is what one did with an armchair.

definitions.meaning: a match or likeness between things

explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence means a close match between things, and also an exchange of mail.
